newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr vols soften despite French elections.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr vols soften despite French elections.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/mark options slipped Friday as they adjusted for weekend time decay, but they remained underpinned before Sunday's second round of French elections, options traders said.

"Everybody is looking to buy options. Nobody is looking to sell anything," said a New York dealer. But he added most of the positioning for the election was conducted earlier in the week, leaving vols to drift today.
Despite an increasingly nervous tone to spot trading this week, dollar/mark has stuck to a tight range, which has capped volatility, traders said.
The spot has weathered a tilt to the left in the first round of France's parliamentary elections and an escalation of tensions between the German government and Bundesbank over asset revaluation.

"Dollar/mark is very quiet from an options standpoint because we are not breaking the ranges," said a Chicago-based dealer for a Canadian bank. "The action, while nervous, has been between 1.69 and 1.71 over the past week, and corporations are pretty well hedged."
Resistance at 1.7150-60 was capping the upside in dollar/mark, the dealer said.

One-month dollar/mark volatility slipped about 0.15 point to 9.65/9.85 percent, while one-year also edged down to 9.3/9.5 percent. One-month 25-delta risk reversals in dollar/mark continued at 0.15 around par.

U.S. dealers said the focus of the options market has been on mark/French and mark/lira as the developments in Europe muddied the outlook for European monetary union. "That's where all of the action is taking place," the Chicago dealer said.
Volatilities for mark crosses were pumped up in the process, dealers said, which could lead to a quick deflation next week.
"As soon as the elections are over I think volatility will come crashing down," said the New York dealer.
Dollar/yen has held to a small range this week while events in Europe took center stage. "It's just following the other dollars," the New York dealer said.

In early afternoon, the dollar was holding around 1.7050 marks and above 116 yen, after firming earlier when New York Federal Reserve Bank President William McDonough said a strong dollar and euro were in the U.S. interest. Also underpinning the dollar were weak U.S. home sales data for April and a rebound in U.S. equities.

One-month dollar/yen volatility was 10.6/10.8 percent, down sharply from 11.3/11.5 percent, and one-year was down 0.2 point at 10.1/10.4 percent. One-month 25-delta risk reversals continued at 1.0/1.3 in favor of yen calls.

Dollar/Canada volatilities were off slightly but still at strong levels as the spot saw choppy trading before Monday's federal elections in Canada. One-week was 6.5/7.5 percent and one-month was 5.1/5.4 percent. Risk reversals were 0.2/0.6 skewed to Canadian dollar calls.
"People are nervous about the downside potential in dollar/Canada," said the Canadian bank dealer.
